args.title: checkout-api: unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy, rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing production health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 0.18. Per the platform runbook, rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was a staging build and also unhealthy, so it was not a rollback candidate).

The first rollback attempt partially failed: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet mixed (us-east v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still v2.3.1). A retry completed the rollout, and all three regions are now on v2.3.0 with status "rolled_out". Post-rollback verification shows the service healthy with error rate down to 0.002.

Follow-up: investigate the root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures before redeploying; the rollout orchestrator error on the first attempt should also be reviewed. Note v2.3.1 never had a healthy production deployment.

trace.final:
The incident was created successfully (the timeout was on the response, not the action) — no duplicate was made.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with a 0.18 error rate. Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy). Note: `v2.3.1-rc` is a *staging* deployment and also unhealthy, so it was not a valid rollback target.

**Rollback target:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release healthy in production.

**Execution:**
1. First rollback attempt failed — `partial_failure`: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1).
2. Retried the rollback and it completed: all three regions now on v2.3.0.
3. Verified: service **healthy**, error rate down from 0.18 → **0.002**.

**Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on checkout-api, documenting the v2.3.1 health-check failures, the rollback to v2.3.0, the partial-failure/retry, and post-rollback verification.

**Follow-ups flagged in the incident:** root-cause the v2.3.1 health-check failures before any redeploy, and review the orchestrator error that caused the first rollout to halt mid-fleet. Also worth noting for the record: v2.3.1 never had a healthy production deployment, so any future attempt to deploy it would require change-manager approval under policy.
